trends.name: Iran Crisis & Oil Supply Shock
trends.summary: Trump administration escalating Iran tensions with explicit threats of military action by tomorrow's 8 PM deadline, potentially triggering major oil supply disruption. PIMCO warns supply shock could translate to growth shock; oil prices already rising and pushing inflation higher while unemployment remains sticky at 4.25%, creating stagflation conditions that paralyze Fed policy.

trends.name: Fed Rate Cut Expectations Collapse
trends.summary: Markets now pricing zero Fed rate cuts as most likely outcome for 2026, with Wells Fargo reversing prior two-cut forecast. Rising inflation from energy prices combined with sticky 4.25% unemployment keeps Fed locked in holding pattern on both sides of dual mandate.

trends.name: Budget Deficit & Fiscal Crisis
trends.summary: PIMCO projects US budget deficits ballooning to ~7% of GDP for 2026, with even a $100bn reduction in supplemental requests yielding only ~6.6%. Massive deficits require constant foreign inflows (particularly Japanese retail) to fund, creating currency and market stability risks.

trends.name: Private Credit Redemption Crisis
trends.summary: Private credit managers like Blue Owl and Cliffwater facing surge in redemption requests triggering domino effect across CLO and credit fund markets. Signals potential liquidity crunch spreading through alternative credit ecosystem with systemic implications.

trends.name: Software Sector Recovery Trade
trends.summary: Software stocks showing signs of bottoming after brutal stretch; three key factors identified for potential rebound including valuation compression and growth re-acceleration. Market positioning for tech sector inflection point with opportunities emerging in AI-adjacent infrastructure plays.

trends.name: AI Infrastructure & Data Center Boom
trends.summary: AI data center and infrastructure plays accelerating with companies like CoreWeave (spending $2.6 for every $1 revenue) and hidden plays like JFrog powering AI code explosion gaining analyst attention. Morgan Stanley highlighting overlooked AI stocks; sector seeing both euphoria and fundamental concerns.

trends.name: S&P 500 Index Composition Shift
trends.summary: Imminent S&P 500 index reconstitution with multiple contenders for inclusion; simultaneously, RSP (equal-weight S&P 500) emerging as strong buy as concentration unwind trade gains momentum. Signals shifting market structure away from mega-cap dominance.

trends.name: Value Stock Rotation & Valuations
trends.summary: Value stocks identified as last hiding place from market turbulence now facing pressure as momentum rotates. Alphabet at 16%+ growth, Nike/On valuations, and Oil energy positioning all creating tactical entry/exit signals as market reassesses growth vs. value tradeoff.

trends.name: Tax Policy & IRS Enforcement Risk
trends.summary: Rising tax avoidance sentiment among Americans claiming protest refusal; simultaneously, IRS actively pursuing unpaid tax liabilities with real consequences for seniors and middle-class. Average refund up $350 YoY; enforcement creating personal finance and macro consumption risks.

trends.name: Energy Sector Divergence & Opportunity
trends.summary: Clean energy stocks gaining technical strength as oil plays face headwinds; $ICLN, $FAN, $TAN showing strength while traditional energy ($XLE, $USO) faces resistance. Kinder Morgan downgraded on pricing concerns; Unusual Machines offering drone boom exposure. Multi-speed energy sector creating tactical opportunities.

trends.name: Japanese Retail Capital Flows & Yen
trends.summary: Japanese retail investors pouring unprecedented savings into US stocks (especially AI plays) to fund current account deficit funding needs. This flow has artificially kept yen weak and US equities bid; reversal could trigger significant market repricing and FX volatility.

trends.name: Trump Geopolitical Friction & Media Control
trends.summary: Trump administration threatening legal action against journalists for national security leaks; simultaneously escalating Iran rhetoric with explicit military threat language. Signals intensifying geopolitical risk, potential market-moving policy shifts, and institutional volatility around executive actions.
